question: He wrote 'Vande Mataram' as a hymn to the motherland. Who is 'he' referred to?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The person who wrote** 'Vande Mataram'** as a hymn to the motherland is **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.**
 
• Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was an** Indian novelist, essayist, and journalist** who wrote in Bengali and is considered one of the key figures in early modern **Bengali literature.**
 
• **'Vande Mataram' **is a poem from **Chattopadhyay's 1882 novel Anandamath**, which was later set to music by** Rabindranath Tagore.**
 
• The song became popular during the Indian independence movement and was widely used as a** patriotic song** and later became the national song of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurobindo Ghosh **was an I**ndian philosopher, yogi, and nationalist** who played a major role in the Indian independence movement. 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru **was the** first Prime Minister of India** and a central figure in Indian politics before and after independence.
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore **was a **Bengali poet, writer, and musician** who was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
